I'm a board-certified dermatologist and a board-certified and fellowship-trained Mohs surgeon. So, I remove skin cancers from people every week in my clinic using the Mohs procedure. The Mohs procedure, which is named after a person, is used in these highly sensitive areas like the nose, the ears, the lips, because the entire purpose is to remove the skin cancer entirely while keeping as much normal skin left behind as absolutely possible. And that's why, in real time, the surgeon is removing the skin cancer, what they see with the naked eye, and taking it into a lab, and then looking at it under the microscope. transcript: C'est une des raisons pour laquelle vous faites de l'acné. L'acné se manifeste le plus souvent par des boutons, des tâches, des pustules, des modules, sur le visage à l'adolescence. La femme adulte qui présente de l'acné doit aller voir en dermatologue car la cause peut être dû au SMOP, anciennement appelé SOPK. Le syndrome métabolique ovarien-poli-endocrinien, anciennement SOPK, peut entraîner de l'acné, de l'hersuitisme, c'est-à-dire des poils au niveau de la barbe chez la femme et une perte de cheveux, avec bien sûr d'autres signes qui peuvent être retrouvés comme une résistance à l'insuline. Il existe plusieurs stades d'acné avec le stade le moins sévère qui se traite avec des produits d'hygiène et des produits de soins. Au stade les plus sévères qui se traite avec de l'iso-tritinoïne ou parfois avec des anti-androgène ou d'autres produits équivalents. C'est pour cela qu'il est préférable de venir consulter chez le dermatologue pour connaître la cause de votre acné et avoir le traitement le plus adapté à votre situation.

transcript: Hi everyone, Dr. Ariel Ostad, cosmetic dermatologist. One of the questions that comes up from patients in the exam room is what is the difference between a lower eyelid blepharoplasty versus using fillers. Lower eyelid blepharoplasty is really used to treat bulges under the skin of the lower eyelids. When people have excessive fat bulges that push forward, those are generally people who are good candidates for removing those fat pads. By making an incision under the lashes or approaching them from inside the eye. There are however many occasions where we can avoid the surgery and use under eye fillers. Those are usually people who have hollows in their lower lid creases. And by loss of collagen in that area, you get some small little what we call herniations which is protrusions of the bulges forward. By injecting a little bit of filler under the eyelids in those creases, we can provide support and therefore push back those fat pads inside and therefore make them less noticeable. So there are instances where eyelid fillers can be used. Eyelid fillers when used appropriately work really well. The key is to inject very small amounts. The results truly last for a couple of years. But yet there are instances where if someone has a severe amount of fat bulges, those have to be surgically removed.

transcript: We invested tens of thousands of pounds into developing our new product, and I told my team that if it didn't work on all hair types, I wasn't launching it. Let me explain. Every hair care brand will tell you their bond repair works. But before I put my name on ours, I needed to see it worked on. That wasn't mine. See, hair damage isn't uniform. Your mid lengths and ends are usually more damaged than the hair at your roots. And what causes that damage is different for everyone. So we tested our formula on 51 people, and I was really specific about who we chose. We had curly, coily, fine and thick hair, heat damage from bleached hair, and hair that had never seen a drop of dye. Our formula combines five different bond technologies, including AI engineered self assembly peptides designed to treat the whole strand, but concentrate where the damage is greater. So if it really did what it was meant to do, it had to work on all of them. When the feedback came in, I was honestly in shock because 82% found their hair looked smoother and 77% said it felt stronger. But as a dermatologist, I wanted to see what was happening inside the strand. In the lab, it reduced breakage by 82% after just one use and repaired 50% of broken bonds in just three minutes. Then we use fluorescence imaging, which lights up the damaged sites inside. After 10 uses, There was 65% fewer damage sites in Caucasian hair and 54% fewer in afro textured hair. So it was cutting deep into the cortex and repairing the damage, not just coating the surface. Seeing the data match what our testers was telling us meant everything to me. But our community has been with us since day one, and honestly, if they didn't love it, I didn't want to launch it. So we handpicked eight of our community insiders to test it before anyone else. And what they told us revealed a lot more than we expected. Follow along, because in part 3, I'm showing you exactly what happened.
